title: The Panassie session, drunk piano and Viva La France
summary: Zutty recounts the Panassie session in which Ladnier got James P. Johnson so drunk he could not play, and Ladnier cheered up the sad Frenchman by saying Viva La France.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And he didn't drink a lot.
We bought that pint of whiskey and old Pandssie, James P. M got so drunk he couldn't do nothing. Couldn't play the piano. And Tommy got him so loaded because he was trying to out-drink me you know.
And they were out of practice eh?

Yes. So that's where that Viva La France came from. (LAUGHTER). Old Tommy looked at Pandssie and say, and he had on a cap and it was cold, he said, 'Viva La France. Because he know that would get that Frenchman's see? So, Pandssie was still looking sad and Tommy said, 'Viva La France I say.' And Pandssie kind of smiled a little and Tommy said, well alright then God damn it.
This is after he and James P. had got drunk was it?
Bunn Teddy Lemonte and Sidney DeParis we had two trumpets on that show at the recording.
I was saying, I think Tommy just got disgusted with.......
